findings.proposed_en:
[§5.6] **Provenance of the run.** Corpus = epoch snapshot `e20260826T060003Z.db` (`sha256` of its first MB `56826f69…`), probe exclusion = none, cut by insertion order, designation with `sha256` checked; all identical to the dose artifact. ⚠️ That corpus **no longer exists**: epoch retention pruned it, and it is not among the four preserved trial databases nor on either host or the author's machine (checked 2026-10-03/04). The run can be re-read from its artifacts but not re-executed on its original input.
[Appendix D, after the table] ⚠️ **The outputs are preserved; the replay input is not.** Every replay artifact above (`c-350*`, `dose-350-v3`, `limiar-17`, `gaps`, `gran-*`, `gran3-*`, `sens-*`) records `e20260826T060003Z.db` as its corpus, and that snapshot was pruned (§5.7.2, §6.2). The measurements on the live database (`superficie.json`, `POOL-ELEGIVEL`, `CHANNEL-ATTRIBUTION`) are likewise tied to a corpus state that no longer exists (the live corpus was 43,255 chunks on 2026-09-30). The artifacts can be audited; they cannot be re-executed bit for bit.

findings.quote_pt: ⚠️ **O controle que valida a comparação com o número publicado:** o braço sem exclusão, rodado no corpus de 30/08, devolve **exatamente 17/350 = 4,86%** — o valor publicado sobre o corpus de 26/08. A troca de corpus não move o teto, logo o braço com exclusão é comparável ao publicado
findings.problem: The control is count-level (17 = 17), in a section whose own finding is that equal counts can hide nearly disjoint sets (17 vs 13, 1 in common). The identity-level check was measured and passes, so the text can now state it.
findings.proposed_en: ⚠️ **The control that makes the comparison with the published number valid — at the level of identity, not count.** The no-exclusion arm, run on the 30/08 corpus, returns 17/350 = 4.86%, the value published on the 26/08 corpus. A matching total alone would be the kind of evidence this section has just disqualified (17 and 13 sensitive states share only one), so the comparison was redone state by state over the existing artifacts (`measurement/sprint-comparabilidade-identidade-572.py`, `COMPARABILITY-IDENTITY-5.7.2.json`). The 350 state keys `(ts, agent, rowid_corte)` coincide 350/350. The sensitive set is the same 17 states, not merely 17 states. In each of the 350 states the ids that would enter and leave are identical. The undosed control arm (the top-10 served at w = 0, which depends on corpus and serve-state but not on the dose) is identical, in order, in 350/350 states (`out/c-350-v3.json` on 26/08 against the 30/08 arm). Changing the corpus moves neither the count, nor which states are sensitive, nor the undosed ranking. The check can see a difference when one exists: applied to the probe-exclusion arm it keeps 1 of 17 sensitive states and 1 of 350 control lists, and a mutation that keeps the count at 17 but changes one entering id makes it fail. Without this control the difference would be attributable to the corpus as much as to the probes. It does not recover the **level** of the ceiling under exclusion on the original corpus, which remains unrecoverable (below).
findings.evidence: python3 measurement/sprint-comparabilidade-identidade-572.py → exit 0; A vs B: L1 350, sensitive 17/17/17 in common, L3 350; C vs B: L4 ordered 350/350; B vs P: 1 in common, L4 1/350; C vs S: L4 350/350; in-memory mutation → exit 1 (L3 349). Output: _sprint-2026-10-04/A-recon-evidence/COMPARABILITY-IDENTITY-5.7.2.json

findings.quote_pt: 🔴 **E o controlo que valida esta comparação verifica a estatística que esta mesma tabela acabou de desqualificar** (acrescentado 2026-09-21, por revisão adversarial).
findings.problem: Open-defect paragraph in the body. The defect is now closed by the identity-level control. Per the manuscript's own convention (Appendix H), closed corrections leave the body.
findings.proposed_en: [Remove from §5.7.2 and add to Appendix H:] **H-x · §5.7.2: the comparability control checked a count, in the section whose finding is that counts do not identify sets.** Adversarial review raised this on 2026-09-21: the control validating the cross-corpus comparison was the equality 17/350 = 17/350, while three lines earlier the same section showed equal totals hiding nearly disjoint sets. It was closed on 2026-10-04 by an identity-level control over the existing artifacts: the same 17 sensitive states, the same entering and leaving ids in 350/350 states, and the same undosed top-10 in 350/350. The control includes a negative control (the exclusion arm breaks identity) and a mutation test. The conclusion did not change; the evidence for it did.
